Sign catalogue

Sign

M59

Looks like: fish

Adapted from the field-cady sign descriptions (Parpola 050). This describes the picture, not the meaning: a sign that looks like a fish may stand for a sound or another word.

Wells W220 · Medial

Appears in 289 texts (381 uses), mostly on seals at Mohenjo-daro; usually sits inside a text. In the larger ICIT corpus its Wells equivalent W220 is in 356 texts, including at Dholavira.

Project finding: “Six” followed by “fish” is a set phrase Solid

Where it appears 289

Counts are distinct texts in the Mahadevan 1977 concordance (a text repeated on many moulded tablets counts once). 369 objects in all carry it.

Project tests 47

Established results

  • “Six” followed by “fish” is a set phraseSolid

    The six-stroke sign and the fish sign appear together far more than chance, like “New York”. A popular idea that “seven + fish” means “seven stars” has almost no support.

    On the findings page · experiments/language/

  • Four small ticks move the fish sign to the endLikely

    A plain fish sign can sit anywhere in a text. Add four small ticks and it usually comes last, so the ticks change how the sign is used, a bit like a word ending.

    On the findings page · experiments/novel_methods/

  • The fish signs are variants of one signLikely

    Six fish-like signs replace each other in the same places and pair with the same neighbours. They behave like forms of one word, not like names of six different gods.

    On the findings page · experiments/core_semantics/

  • Whether M87 stands in for the fish M59 cannot be tested at this corpus sizeCan’t test yet

    The method found 2% of planted stand-ins; M87 sits next to the fish rather than in its slot.

    experiments/parpola_rules34/RESULTS.md
